newsitem.title: USA: Water-treatment plant reopens at Alaska oil port.
newsitem.headline: Water-treatment plant reopens at Alaska oil port.

text.p: A ballast-water treatment plant at Alaska's Valdez port reopened at 1000 Alaska time/1900 GMT Wednesday, allowing oil tankers to resume their loading schedules, a U.S. Coast Guard official said.
"(The plant's) come back on a temporary basis," said Lieutenant Commander Joe McGuiness.
The plant, which treats ballast water from oil tankers, closed over the weekend after officials discovered an oil slick in the port.
Officials later determined the plant caused the slick, McGuiness said.
Arriving tankers were required to retain their ballast water - which they need for balance on their way to Alaska.
Since the plant shut, a handful of tankers left Valdez with partial crude oil cargoes or waited for the plant to return.
Coast Guard officials said yesterday three tankers were berthed at the port's docks.
But early Wednesday, traffic appeared to return to normal.
"As of 0730 (1630 GMT) there was one ship," berthed to load crude oil, said a oil terminal official.
Coast Guard officials confirmed two other ships, the Overseas Juno and the Overseas Washington, operated by BP America, left overnight.
The remaining ship was Arco's Alaska tanker.
Tankers scheduled to arrive near-term included: Overseas Alaska, Arco Juno, Arco Indepedence, and Sea River's North Slope, the Coast Guard said.
